Agreement to run a dedicated 4-hour tail-latency benchmark and deliver an updated cost model + pilot dashboard. Redwood to propose a modest capacity bump for peak window and share security docs.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-17 10:00 PT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (HarborLine Head of ML), Omar (Infra), Lena (Prod)

Summary (auto): Quick check of last 48h run. Key metric: tokens per dollar and tokens/sec/$ improving with KV cache and prompt templating but tail latency spikes during bursts. Action: run targeted tail-latency benchmark, share updated cost model.

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to about 40 minutes, agenda — quick results review, then tuning suggestions, then next steps.
01:02 Priya: thanks, Maya, yea we've got a hard deadline end of quarter to justify the pilot spend, so today we want numbers i can take to finance.
01:28 Jonah: cool we pulled the last 48 hours from the pilot cluster — ran with the v2-medium quantized model and enabling prefix cache on the 3 heaviest prompts. hit rates went from ~12% to ~46% on those templated prompts. that shows in tokens/sec per dollar.
02:10 Omar: just to clarify, templating means we replaced the free-form customer text with the prompt slot pattern, right? not changing output length?
02:23 Jonah: yeah exactly, prefix normalization so we get better cache reuse. we didn't shorten responses, just normalized the input shape.
03:05 Lena: are we sure that improvement is general? some of our dialogs are more free-form.
03:20 Jonah: good point, for free-form cases hit-rate is lower. we recommended a hybrid: template the top 20 most frequent flows, leave longform as untemplated. overall the average tokens/sec/$ improved by ~38% across the dataset.
04:10 Priya: show me the raw numbers — tokens per dollar and also tokens/sec.
04:20 Jonah: yep link is in the deck: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/harborline-06-17 (note: internal link). in short, baseline hosted run: 1.8k tokens/sec per GPU at $X yields ~Y tokens per dollar; with caching and 8-request batching we saw effective tokens/sec of 2.4k and token/$ up ~38%.
05:10 Omar: latency — what's p95 and p99 doing under that batching level?
05:24 Jonah: p50 is fine, sub-120ms. p95 crept to ~520ms with 8-request batching and shared KV cold misses. p99 spikes to 1.6s in burst periods.
06:00 Priya: 1.6s p99 is pretty high for our product UX, we need to show finance that avg cost drops without wrecking SLA.
06:18 Maya: right — tradeoff conversation. there are a few knobs: smaller batching during peak interactive, adaptive batching, and aggressive prefix caching. also can look at model variant: a slightly smaller quantized model gives lower p99 but a bit worse quality.
07:00 Omar: is the KV cache warm-up the main cause of p99 on bursts?
07:12 Jonah: mostly. when a new user flow hits a node with a cold KV set, the kernel incurs extra overhead. our recommendation: 1) pre-warm cache for top flows, 2) add a short-lived local LRU to avoid cross-node misses, 3) consider slightly higher reserved concurrency for peak windows.
08:00 Priya: what's the unit econ if we pre-warm caches? does it change tokens/$ materially considering the extra memory cost?
08:18 Jonah: pre-warm is effectively free from token perspective; memory is tiny compared to GPU cost. trading some memory for cache hit increases tokens per dollar — in our run it moved tokens/$ another +10% when pre-warm was enabled for top 20 flows.
09:05 Lena: any impact on cold start of new model variants? we may A/B test smaller quantized model vs base.
09:22 Jonah: smaller quantized variant reduces latency 10–20% p95 but you lose ~3–5% on quality metrics. depends on whether classification/regression downstream tolerates it.
10:10 Priya: can we quantify cost savings if we go with adaptive batching? like only batch during low conc but drop to batch size 2 during peak.
10:26 Jonah: yes. our simulator shows adaptive batching yields almost same tokens/$ as static batch 8 during low usage but keeps p95 ~200–350ms during spikes — net econ about -5% tokens/$ compared to static batch 8 but much better tail latency.
11:00 Maya: that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. for HarborLine we suggested a mixed policy: adaptive batching + prefix caching + canary smaller model for edge flows.
12:05 Omar: what about dedicated capacity? is that still cost-favorable?
12:20 Maya: for predictable high throughput, Dedicated can lower per-token price if you commit. based on your projected peak windows, we estimated break-even in ~45 days of 24/7 throughput at current traffic. short pilots rarely justify dedicated unless you need isolation/SLA.
13:00 Priya: we might need isolation for compliance, but not sure yet. for the pilot decision today we care more about tokens/$ and UX.
13:28 Jonah: noted. we also ran a quantization sweep — int8 vs int4 configs — the int4 had more variability in tail latency under heavy KV misses. int8 is more stable for now.
14:05 Omar: so recommendation is int8 for pilot, evaluate int4 after cache is stable?
14:12 Jonah: exactly. int8 + prefix caching + adaptive batching.
15:00 Priya: any immediate quick wins we can do on our side this week?
15:07 Maya: yes — 3 things: 1) apply templating to your top 20 prompts (Omar to share examples), 2) opt-in to the pre-warm list for top flows, 3) allow Redwood to run a 4h tail-latency benchmark during your low-traffic window.
15:40 Omar: i can provide prompt lists and traffic histogram by tomorrow.
15:52 Priya: schedule the benchmark on thursday afternoon pacific please.
16:10 Jonah: i'll put together a runbook and test harness, with synthetic replays and real token samples, we'll also instrument per-node KV hit metrics.
17:00 Maya: finance will ask for a simple model — net tokens per dollar and projected monthly cost at current volumes. we'll send an updated spreadsheet.
17:30 Lena: also add a sensitivity column showing the effect of 10%/20% traffic spikes.
18:10 Maya: yes will do.
19:00 Priya: security — we need SOC2 artifact and encryption details for the pilot.
19:18 Maya: will share the SOC2 + encryption + SSO flow doc. jumping a bit — Jonah, any concerns about RBAC or audit logs?
19:40 Jonah: nothing blocking, audit logs are available in the console, and we can ship a limited retention copy for the pilot. minor note: if HarborLine wants HSM for key management that's an enterprise add-on.
20:30 Omar: forward that HSM add-on info; we're evaluating KMS options.
21:00 Maya: we'll attach links in the follow up.
21:30 Priya: question on competitor comparison — we've been evaluating Anthropic but their cost model is different. any notes?
21:50 Maya: Anthropic does some gen quality claims, but in our experience, the unit economics vary; we'll include a short competitor note but not a deep comparison.
22:30 Priya: okay.
22:45 Jonah: quick note on bench methodology: our tokens/$ uses GPU-hour cost + per-request overheads; we include prefix cache savings as token avoidance, not discounted unit price. that keeps the model conservative.
23:40 Omar: conservative is fine. we want defensible numbers.
24:00 Maya: timeline recap: Jonah runs bench on Thu, Maya sends cost model Wed, Omar provides prompts Tue, Priya confirms stakeholder by next Monday.
25:10 Lena: can you also include a visualization of tokens/sec/$ vs p95 in the dashboard? that's what product wants to see.
25:32 Jonah: yes the pilot dashboard already has a tokens/sec vs latency panel, i'll expose that to HarborLine. link will be in mail.
26:10 Priya: any issue with data retention? for pilot we need logs kept for 30 days.
26:18 Maya: default is 14, we can set 30 for pilot under retention opt-in. will note in follow up.
27:00 Omar: what about the suggestion to bump reserved concurrency for the 9–11am slot, does that require contract change?
27:14 Maya: small temporary bump can be done under pilot terms, we'll propose a nominal capacity uplift and price it as a temporary add-on.
28:05 Priya: let's see the numbers first.
28:30 Jonah: also found one micro-optimization: using a trimmed KV key (remove user-specific salts) improved cross-user cache hits slightly but we need to ensure privacy constraints.
29:00 Omar: careful on that one, our privacy team will want to sign off.
29:18 Maya: noted — include privacy review as part of the security artifact share.
30:10 Priya: ok final questions?
30:20 Lena: is there a recommended SLA to aim for if we want to push to Dedicated later?
30:30 Maya: typical Dedicated SLA targets are 99.9% p95 under committed throughput; we can model that once we see the tail-latency run.
31:05 Jonah: scheduling note — i'll need a 2 hour window to warm nodes before the 4h bench to simulate realistic cache state.
31:30 Omar: that works for thursday afternoon; i'll confirm exact time.
32:00 Maya: perfect.
32:15 Priya: thanks everyone. quick recap from my side: we want the conservative cost model, dashboard, tail-latency run, and SOC2 docs.
32:40 Maya: exactly. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.
33:05 Jonah: action checklist in the chat now.
33:20 Omar: thanks all.
34:00 [meeting ends — recording stops]
